# Reverse linked list in fixed-size groups

<!-- meta:begin -->

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/reverse-linked-list-in-fixed-size-groups)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

Given an array `values` containing a singly linked list’s values in head-to-tail order, and an integer `k` with $$k \ge 1$$, reverse every complete consecutive block of `k` nodes. If a final block contains fewer than `k` nodes, leave it unchanged.

The reversal must be performed in place — do not build a separate copy of the data as the primary technique. Return the transformed list as an array of values.

Example 1:

```text
Input: values = [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16], k = 3

Output: [6, 4, 2, 12, 10, 8, 14, 16]
```

Explanation: The full blocks `[2, 4, 6]` and `[8, 10, 12]` are reversed, while the remaining block `[14, 16]` has fewer than three elements and stays unchanged.



Example 2:

```text
Input: values = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17], k = 4

Output: [7, 5, 3, 1, 15, 13, 11, 9, 17]
```

Explanation: Each complete group of four is reversed. The final single-element block `[17]` is left in its original position because it is too small to reverse.

Example 3:

```text
Input: values = [9, 8, 7, 6, 5], k = 5

Output: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
```

Explanation: The entire array forms one full group of size five, so the whole list is reversed.

Constraints:

* Let `n = values.length`; then $$1 \le n \le 200000$$
* $$k \ge 1$$
* If $$k > n$$, no block is reversed and the array remains unchanged.
* The intended solution runs in $$O(n)$$ time.
* Use $$O(1)$$ extra space; the recursion call stack is not counted against this bound.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Process the list one block of k nodes at a time, reversing each full block and leaving a short tail untouched.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use the standard iterative three-pointer reversal within each block, reconnecting the previous block's tail to the new head.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Before reversing a block, verify it has exactly k nodes, the final partial block must remain in original order.

</details>
